title: Duel verdict
description: One judge, one blind pairwise comparison. The judge sees a rubric and two candidates and nothing else — no lineage, no authorship, no incumbency. 'none' is a verdict, not a failure: it is what keeps a split panel from being read as a decision.

winner.description: Which candidate the rubric prefers, or none when nothing separates them.

separating_criterion.description: The first rubric criterion that separated the candidates. Absent when nothing did.

pointed.description: Concrete places in the candidates that decided it. A preference that points at nothing is taste, not judgment, and is rejected by the caller.
